title: Promoting Travel, Commerce, and National Security Act of 2016
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The summary has been expanded because action occurred on the measure.)

Promoting Travel, Commerce, and National Security Act of 2016

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the federal criminal code to allow the United States to prosecute certain U.S. employees who engage in conduct in Canada that would constitute a federal criminal offense if the conduct had occurred in the United States. This bill applies to a Department of Homeland Security or Department of Justice employee, contractor, or employee of a contractor who is stationed in Canada pursuant to a border security initiative.

summary.headline: A 2016 law lets the U.S. prosecute certain federal employees and contractors stationed in Canada for conduct that would be a federal crime in the United States.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes the federal criminal code so that certain U.S. personnel working in Canada can be charged in the United States. The conduct must be something that would be a federal crime if it happened in the U.S. The law covers Department of Homeland Security and Department of Justice employees, contractors, and contractor employees who are stationed in Canada under a border security initiative. The summary does not describe any other changes.

who_it_affects.group: Department of Homeland Security and Department of Justice employees stationed in Canada under a border security initiative
who_it_affects.how: They can be prosecuted in the United States for conduct in Canada that would be a federal crime if committed in the U.S.

who_it_affects.group: Contractors and contractor employees stationed in Canada under a border security initiative
who_it_affects.how: They can be prosecuted in the United States for conduct in Canada that would be a federal crime if committed in the U.S.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on December 16, 2016. The official summary does not describe a separate later start date.
